name: Brazil 1970 (FIFA World Cup, Mexico)
scopeNote: Brazil at the 1970 World Cup, six matches (Czechoslovakia 3 Jun 4-1, England 7 Jun 1-0, Romania 10 Jun 3-2, Peru 14 Jun 4-2, Uruguay 17 Jun 3-1, Italy 21 Jun 4-1) under Mário Zagallo, who took over after Saldanha's dismissal in March 1970 (16 or 17 March by source). Re-research: v1 sources kept, new evidence added. WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS. Possession/build-up: Opta data (The Analyst) says Brazil 'averaged far more sequences of 10 passes or more than any other team at the 1970 finals' and calls the Italy final goal 'a patient build-up, then devastating speed'; Bleacher Report says Brazil 'craved possession' and dominated the ball against Italy, who did not press. Brazil also scored from counters (Tostão: Clodoaldo started the 4th goal on a counter-attack) and Zagallo himself said Europeans liked space to counter, so he set up to mark from midfield and then leave with up to seven players. No possession percentage figures were found. Defence: Zagallo's own retrospective account (via Milton Leite's book) is a midfield block, 'todo mundo voltava para marcar', not pressing the opponent's build-up; only Brito, Piazza and Everaldo did not go forward. Brazil conceded 7 goals in 6 matches (Bleacher Report), and the Italy equaliser came from a Brito error (These Football Times). Brazil's own marking scheme (zonal vs man) is NOT stated explicitly in any read source; the opponents' man-marking (Italy, with slides of their defenders prepared by Parreira and Rogério and Zagallo using table-football buttons, per Carlos Alberto; Pelé's 'the avenue'; Tostão and Jairzinho agreeing who follows the full-back) is well documented, and Zagallo's reaction was to rotate attackers to drag markers out of position. Zagallo's role: sources disagree on whether he imposed a system or freed the stars. Evidence for system: his own 4-3-3 insistence over Saldanha's 4-2-4, moving Piazza to centre-back and Clodoaldo in, cutting Dirceu Lopes, asking for a centre-forward (Tostão: 'um grande estrategista'), preparing Italy-specific movements, and a scientific physical programme (Chirol, Parreira, Coutinho, Carlesso; 21 days at altitude in Guanajuato). Evidence for talent-led: Bleacher Report says Zagallo 'realized that his role was one of overall management, not specific tactics'; These Football Times argues expressiveness came 'by chance, rather than design' and that he was 'swept along' by Mexico 70. Both views are in the file; none is chosen. Zagallo was 39 (Leite) and he spoke of his respect from veteran players. Squad age figures were not found. LABELS: formation labels disagree: 4-3-3 (Zagallo, Tostão), 4-2-4 (Saldanha's qualifiers; some sources), 4-5-1 (Zagallo per Leite, rendered '1-4-5-1'), 'false 4-3-3' (Coaches' Voice), and 4-4-1-1 defending (Coaches' Voice). The 'Five 10s' phrase is credited to Jairzinho and ESPN and was a selection fact; Gérson/Tostão/Rivellino roles were not pure 10s (Tostão: 'facilitador dos gols'). WHERE THIN: no FIFA Technical Study Group report for 1970 was found online; no Zonal Marking, Spielverlagerung or Wilson/Cox text was readable (Wilson's Guardian/book pages not found; Medium summary 403); no Brazil possession percentages; no 1970 contemporary press pieces on marking beyond Trivela reprints; Tostão/Carlos Alberto/Zagallo recollections are 30-50 years later (retrospectiveOnly). Dates are exact to the match day where the source names a match; otherwise the month.
openQuestions: Brazil's own marking scheme (zonal vs man) is not stated in any read source; Zagallo describes a midfield block, not a scheme type.
Saldanha dismissal date: 16 vs 17 March 1970 (Jornal Opção says April, after a Bangu draw, which conflicts).
Formation label: 4-3-3 (Zagallo, Tostão), 4-2-4, 4-5-1 (Leite), 4-4-1-1 in defence (Coaches' Voice).
Who marked Pelé for Italy (Bertini vs Burgnich) differs between sources; Pelé's header was over Burgnich per Gaceta/other accounts.
Zagallo as system-imposer (Tostão, Leite, Carlos Alberto) vs facilitator of talent (Bleacher Report, These Football Times) is unresolved.
FIFA Technical Study Group report and independent tier A tactical analysis (Zonal Marking, Spielverlagerung, Wilson, Cox) not found.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Piazza was a central midfielder who had been called up by Saldanha to play in his preferred position. Once Zagallo took over, however, he was moved back to play as a central defender. The idea was that Piazza's ability on the ball would improve the team’s build-up play from deep.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: The build-up started with Piazza, who linked with Clodoaldo or one of the full-backs – mostly Carlos Alberto on the right. Further forward, the team looked for its chief playmaker and often the deepest of the front five: Gérson.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Ahead of Clodoaldo, the team's single pivot, Zagallo selected a group of five attacking players who constantly interchanged positions.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: When facing more structured attacks by their opponents, Brazil set up with a much lower block and dropped into a defensive shape more resembling a 4-4-1-1.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: The back four would start a few metres from the penalty area, with Gérson dropping alongside Clodoaldo into a midfield two ahead of them. Rivelino and Jairzinho would defend the wide areas, leaving Tostão as the attacking pivot and Pelé ahead of him.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: a covering back line of three – both centre-backs and usually Everaldo, the less attacking full-back would push up as high as the halfway line. Clodoaldo would generally sit just in front of them.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: When they then won the ball back, Gérson was the player to whom they looked. A fine technician, he was capable of launching a quick counter-attack or holding possession while the team reorganised into its offensive shape.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: That left a lot of space in behind on transition. For all their offensive prowess, this was a team that conceded both chances and goals. The seven goals they conceded in six games is more than any subsequent World Cup winners have conceded in the 12 tournaments since 1970.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: He knew that the Mexican heat would make it almost impossible for teams to sustain high-pressing tactics against them.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Zagallo had built a team to defend with the ball, however.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: A back line of four was constant, with full-backs pushed forward to attack almost as wingers. The attacking midfielders in front of them moved from out to in, seeking goalscoring positions.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: A quick and efficient switch from one flank to another results in a stunning low finish from an advancing full-back.

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: “I want discipline and order, will and self-sacrifice from all of you,” he reportedly said in his first meeting with members of the team led by Pelé

sources.title: Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Zagallo also wanted to compress the pitch as much as possible in the defensive phase.

statedView.quote: Não me afastaria um centímetro da minha ideia geral de jogo, que podem classificar de 4-3-3 anterior.

statedView.quote: Se fôssemos disputar o jogo final da Copa, Gérson e Rivellino jogariam. Mas como ainda temos muito esforço pela frente, acho preferível não expor ninguém à hipótese de ter sua contusão agravada
I want discipline and order, will and self-sacrifice from all of you

Era um time em que todo mundo voltava para marcar, só o Tostão ficava um pouco mais à frente. Armei assim porque os times europeus gostavam de ter espaço para contra-atacar. Por isso, a marcação era a partir do meio-campo e não lá na frente, pressionando a saída de bola deles.

statedView.quote: O time tinha ido bem nas eliminatórias jogando no 4-2-4, mas para uma Copa do Mundo aquilo era um retrocesso, pois em 1958 e 1962 nós já tínhamos jogado num 4-3-3
